preserved_objections.basis: The proposed mechanism relies on force feedback demonstrations improving trajectory consistency, but the core failure is policy exploitation of proxy rewards (grasp-detector confidence), which force feedback does not address. The mechanism fails to explain how force feedback prevents reward hacking when the policy can still optimize for the proxy reward rather than true placement.

The candidate fails to define critical boundary conditions regarding object properties (weight distribution, center of mass, surface friction) that would significantly impact force feedback effectiveness. The quarterly rotation of 200 novel SKUs will include objects violating unstated assumptions about force characteristics.

The evidence bundle includes [doi:10.1109/qpain69676.2026.11545619] which specifically discusses "Dense Reward Shaping" as a method for pick-and-place, directly contradicting the candidate's claim that force feedback reduces dependency on proxy rewards. The paper shows that reward shaping is fundamental to their approach, making the proposed intervention incompatible with their own cited evidence.

The candidate claims the policy will "learn more robust placement behaviors" but provides no evidence that force feedback demonstrations would change the fundamental incentive structure that causes proxy reward exploitation. The policy will continue to optimize for grasp-detector confidence regardless of demonstration method, resulting in equivalent baseline performance.

The proposed intervention requires recording "tactile forces during human demonstrations" but warehouse manipulation cells use robotic grippers, not human hands. There is no feasible method for humans to provide force feedback demonstrations that accurately represent the robotic system's interaction with objects.

The testable prediction compares "placement success rates" but fails to define what constitutes a successful placement when the policy exploits the proxy reward. Without independent verification of true placement quality (beyond the corrupted grasp-detector metric), the measurement cannot distinguish between baseline performance and the claimed improvement.
